title: Triangular resigning of a mapping complex into a finite total
statement:
Let $\mathcal E$ be an abelian category in a fixed morphism universe [def-sp-abelian, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $P,I$ be cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with $P^i=0$ for $i>0$ and $I^r=0$ for $r<0$. Write $P_p=P^{-p}$ and $\partial_{p+1}=d_P^{-p-1}$. Define a complex of abelian groups $C$ by
$$C^n=\prod_{p\geq0}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal E}(P_p,I^{n-p}),\qquad \delta x=d_Ix-(-1)^nx\partial.$$
Only $0\leq p\leq n$ contribute, and $C^n=0$ for $n<0$. Define the commuting first-quadrant double complex of abelian groups $H^{p,r}=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal E}(P_p,I^r)$ with horizontal differential $x\mapsto x\partial_{p+1}$ and vertical differential $x\mapsto d_Ix$, and its total differential $d_h+(-1)^p d_I$ [def-sp-double-complex-total]. Then the bidegree formula
$$T(x)_{p,r}=t(p,r)x_{p,r},\qquad t(p,r)=(-1)^{pr+p(p+1)/2}$$
defines a cochain isomorphism $T:C\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tot}H$, and hence the specified isomorphism $Q(C)\cong Q(\operatorname{Tot}H)$ in $D(\operatorname{Ab})$. Its inverse uses the same multipliers. In particular $\delta^2=0$ and $T\delta=d_{\operatorname{Tot}}T$. The multiplier satisfies
$$t(p,r+1)=(-1)^pt(p,r),\qquad (-1)^{p+r+1}t(p+1,r)=t(p,r).$$
For every $n\geq0$, $\delta x=0$ is exactly the cochain-map condition for the family $x:P\to I[n]$. For such maps $u,v$ and a chain homotopy $H$ with convention $u-v=d_{I[n]}H+Hd_P$, the same family $H$ belongs to $C^{n-1}$ and $u-v=(-1)^n\delta H$. Thus $T(u)-T(v)=(-1)^n d_{\operatorname{Tot}}T(H)$, including $n=0$ where $C^{-1}=0$. No injectivity, projectivity or exactness of a Hom functor is assumed.

proof.text: Retain the explicit commuting Hom bicomplex. Its objects are zero outside the first quadrant because either the source P^(-p) or the target I^r is zero. Prove that restriction to the nonpositive source degrees is bijective: equality is detected on those coordinates, and the inverse inserts zero maps in the positive source degrees. Define the signed finite diagonal sum A_n and signed coordinate projection S_n explicitly. Projection onto one diagonal coordinate kills every other inclusion. Thus S_n A_n is the identity, using t(p,r)^2=1 on surviving components and zero source or target elsewhere. Conversely, test A_n S_n on each coproduct inclusion; exactly one summand survives, while summands outside the first quadrant are zero. This proves both inverse identities, including negative total degrees.

source.place: Tag 010V, section-complexes: cochain-complex equations; direct expansion of the stated differential.

proof.text: For e(p,r)=pr+p(p+1)/2 prove e(p,r+1)=p+e(p,r). The identity (p+1)(p+2)=p(p+1)+2(p+1) gives the exact integer-division identity (p+1)(p+2)/2=p(p+1)/2+p+1. Hence e(p+1,r)=e(p,r)+p+r+1. Apply Int.negOnePow_add and Int.negOnePow_two_mul to obtain both recurrences. The calculation works for all integer p and r; each multiplier squares to one by Int.units_mul_self.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: agent-written sign normalization for the extracted internal-bar argument.

proof.text: Verify the cochain identity for the signed projection maps S first, using the universal property of the total coproduct. On its (p,r) inclusion, the total differential is the sum of the horizontal inclusion applied to precomposition with d_P and the vertical inclusion applied to (-1)^p postcomposition with d_I. Apply HomComplex.δ_v and check a source coordinate -q. When q=p the vertical recurrence gives equality. When q=p+1 the horizontal recurrence, multiplied by the sign again, gives equality. In every other coordinate all terms are zero. This proves S_n followed by δ equals d followed by S_(n+1), without boundedness assumptions. Using the two inverse identities from step 1 and cancelling S_(n+1) yields the requested cochain identity for A.

source.place: Tag 012Z, definition-associated-simple-complex: horizontal plus signed vertical differential; explicit comparison with step 3.

proof.text: Package A_n and S_n into degreewise isomorphisms using the two proved inverse identities. HomologicalComplex.Hom.isoOfComponents and step 4 give the cochain isomorphism T, with exactly the specified finite-sum and projection formulas. Apply DerivedCategory.Q.mapIso to T. Its hom and inverse are definitionally Q.map T.hom and Q.map T.inv, as required.

source.place: Tag 05RU, definition-unbounded-derived-category: localization; explicit functorial inverse identities.

proof.text: Use Mathlib CochainComplex.HomComplex.Cocycle.equivHomShift. Its underlying cochain is exactly homTotalMapFamily. A cochain x with δx=0 gives the cocycle Cocycle.mk x, whose inverse image is a map to I[n]. Conversely the image of any such map is a cocycle. This proves both directions, in fact for every integer n.

source.place: Tags 010V and 011G: section-complexes and definition-shift-cochain; direct substitution.

proof.text: Apply HomComplex.Cochain.δ_rightUnshift to Cochain.ofHomotopy H, followed by HomComplex.δ_ofHomotopy. Multiplication by n.negOnePow twice cancels, and rightUnshift preserves subtraction, so the displayed map-family difference equals n.negOnePow times δ of the homotopy family. Apply the additive degree-n comparison map, use map_zsmul and the proved cochain identity in degree n-1, and obtain the total homotopy formula. The zero and negative degree cases are included in the same calculation; the degree -1 vanishing follows from step 1. No projectivity, injectivity or exactness of Hom is used.
